title: Dan Hicks, who called memorable moments across sports world for NBC, dies at 64
content:
Dan Hicks, a prominent play-by-play voice for NBC Sports who spent more 30 years narrating some of the sports world’s biggest moments, from major golf tournaments to Olympic swimming pools, died Wednesday, his wife,Hannah Storm, said in a statement. He was 64.

Hicks had been married to Storm, a longtime “SportsCenter” anchor, since 1994. She said in her statement Thursday that his death was “sudden and unexpected,” though she did not say where he died.

“Dan was truly one of a kind and, quite simply, the person everyone wanted to be around,” Storm said. “When he walked into a room, he brought the energy, the laughter and the people together. He was endlessly kind, thoughtful and funny, and he made everyone feel like they mattered.”

Hicks was to call Notre Dame’s game this Saturday against Boston College, according to an NBC schedule released earlier this week.

Hicks joined NBC Sports in 1992 after a short stint with CNN. With NBC, he served as play-by-play commentator for Notre Dame football games, contributed to NFL coverage, was a sideline reporter on “NBA on NBC,” and played a key role in the network’s golf and Olympics coverage.

Among his most memorable calls were a U.S. comeback the 4×100 freestyle relay at the Beijing Olympics, which secured Michael Phelps’ eighth gold medal of the Games, and when Tiger Woods sunk a 12-foot putt to force a playoff at the 2008 U.S. Open.

“Expect anything different?” Hicks calmly voiced as Woods pumped his fists and the Torrey Pines crowd roared.

In a statement Thursday, the PGA Tour called Hicks’ work with commentator Johnny Miller “one of golf television’s defining broadcast partnerships.”

“Dan Hicks was an extraordinary colleague, friend and person,” NBC News said in a statement. “He was an exceptional storyteller and caller of games and events who elevated some of the biggest moments in sports history.”

Hicks — who was born in Greenwich, Conn., and later graduated from the University of Arizona — became NBC’s lead play-by-play golf announcer in 2000.

“Partner,” Hicks told Miller after the 2014 U.S. Open, when NBC’s broadcasting rights to the tournament were ending, “it’s been a great ride.”

This story will be updated.
